subject: Interim uptime benchmark waiver & fixed monthly credit schedule
messages:
From: Samir Khan <samir.k@acme-systems.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: ops-legal <legal@acme-systems.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Request: interim uptime benchmark waiver + proposal for flat monthly credit

Rachel — thanks for the time on Tuesday. Quick follow up here with a concrete ask so our procurement and SRE teams can move forward.

High level request: for the first 90 days after go-live we need Redwood to accept an interim uptime benchmark of 99.7% (instead of the standard 99.95%) because our usage pattern and risk profile during their migration window will create a higher probability of short, regional interruptions. We understand this is an exception; we want to make it operationally simple and bounded.

What we propose instead of a permanent baseline change: a fixed monthly credit schedule for the pilot period that provides the customer with predictable remediation if we hit degraded service. Proposed structure from our side (open to your counter):
- If uptime >= 99.7%: no credit
- 99.5% — 99.699%: flat $10,000 monthly credit
- 99.0% — 99.499%: flat $25,000 monthly credit
- <99.0%: escalate to full SLA remediation (per contract)

We can share our maintenance calendar (attached) and are asking that scheduled regional maintenance windows be excluded from the pilot calculations (we'll list them ahead of time).

Attached: opsplaybook-maintenance-log.csv with planned maint windows for Q1.

Can Redwood legal/ops confirm whether you can accept an interim waiver framed as this 90-day pilot with a fixed credit schedule instead of adjusting the baseline? If not, what's the minimum counter you'd be willing to consider?

Thanks — Samir
Samir Khan
Head of Cloud Ops, Acme Systems
[sent from mobile]
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.k@acme-systems.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 13:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: interim uptime benchmark waiver + proposal for flat monthly credit

Samir — appreciate the clear proposal and the attachment. Short answer: we are open to a bounded pilot but need to protect platform economics and other customers. Two immediate thoughts:

1) Baseline vs. carveout: we prefer keeping the standard baseline (99.95%) and instead define a temporary maintenance carveout + a capped fixed monthly credit during the pilot. That keeps the canonical SLA intact while giving Acme predictable remediation.

2) Credit cap & monitoring: we can accept a 90-day pilot with a fixed credit schedule, but we need a monthly cap and objective monitoring signals we both can access. Proposed Redwood counter:
- Pilot length: 90 days from production cutover
- Maintenance carveouts: scheduled regional windows pre-notified 14 days in advance (we'll exclude those from the measurement window)
- Fixed credit schedule (Redwood counter):
  - 99.7% — 99.949%: $12,500/month (cap)
  - 99.5% — 99.699%: $30,000/month (cap)
  - <99.5%: escalate to contract remedies (but we will not exceed $60,000/month in credits for the pilot period overall)
- Access: we will provide a read-only dashboard with the uptime/latency measurement for the pilot so both sides can reconcile quickly

Next steps: I'll loop in Laura from legal to confirm the carveout language and the cap mechanics. If Acme signs the pilot appendix we'll put the pilot into effect at cutover. Can you confirm the proposed 14-day notification cadence for scheduled maintenance and whether your procurement team will accept a credit-cap structure?

Attachment: acme-sla-draft-v3.pdf (redwood edits annotated)

Best,
Rachel Kim
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: internal: Acme pilot — legal/finance check on pilot cap & carveouts

Rachel — quick internal note so we all align before I respond to Acme/legal. Key risk items and recommended guardrails:

- Risk: dropping the baseline creates precedence. We avoid that by keeping 99.95% in the master SLA and adding a pilot appendix.
- Cap: $60k/month cap for the pilot is reasonable given ARR and mitigates open liability; would prefer language that ties credits to invoice reduction (account-level credit memo) not cash payouts.
- Scheduled maintenance: 14-day pre-notification is fine if Acme commits to a rolling calendar (we need named windows; a list in the appendix is better than ad-hoc messages).
- Measurement: the dashboard + mutual reconciliation window (7 business days post-month) is required. If there's a dispute, we propose a one-time independent metric audit during the pilot (cost split 50/50) — call this out.
- Termination: pilot auto-ends at 90 days unless both parties mutually agree to extend. If performance is consistently <99.5% for two consecutive months, we should allow Redwood to propose remediation steps (capacity bump/architecture changes) before escalating credits further.

I'll draft a short appendix with the above and circulate by EOD Monday. If Marissa/Connor have objections on the numbers or the credit accounting treatment, flag them now.

-L
Laura Bennett
Deputy Head, Legal & Contracts
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.k@acme-systems.com>
Cc: legal@acme-systems.com, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: interim uptime benchmark waiver + proposal for flat monthly credit

Samir — thanks. After internal review we can accept a 90-day pilot under these terms (summary below). If that matches Acme's expectation we'll ask Procurement to sign the pilot appendix and schedule the production cutover.

Pilot summary (agreed in principle):
- Pilot length: 90 days from production cutover
- Baseline: canonical SLA remains 99.95%; pilot is implemented via an appendix only
- Maintenance carveouts: Acme will provide a list of planned regional windows 14 days prior; those windows are excluded from monthly uptime calc for pilot
- Credit schedule (caps apply):
  - 99.7% — 99.949% uptime: Redwood issues a $12,500 credit (account credit memo)
  - 99.5% — 99.699% uptime: Redwood issues a $30,000 credit (account credit memo)
  - <99.5%: follow standard contract remedies; Redwood reserves the right to propose remediation steps before additional credits
- Monthly credit cap: $60,000 (total credits applied during any single pilot month will not exceed this amount)
- Measurement & reconciliation: read-only dashboard + 7-business-day reconciliation window; one-time independent audit if disputed (cost split 50/50)
- Termination/extension: auto-ends at 90 days unless mutually agreed

Please confirm 'yes' to these bullet points and we will circulate the appendix (Laura will send an initial draft). Also propose a 30-minute kickoff on Wed next week to align SREs and set monitoring access.
